title: Genomic epidemiology reconstructs the pre-detection transmission and establishment of chikungunya virus in Guangdong, China
abstract: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the 2025 chikungunya outbreak in southern China, which resulted in over 25,000 confirmed cases. The research aimed to reconstruct the origins and transmission dynamics of the outbreak using genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data. The study generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and traced the outbreak to a single introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) lineage. The findings revealed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission patterns, highlighting the limitations of passive surveillance in detecting early outbreaks. These results demonstrate the importance of genomic surveillance in understanding and responding to emerging chikungunya epidemics, particularly in regions at the edge of endemic transmission. The study's evidence is strong, as it is based on genomic data and spatiotemporal analysis, but its generalizability may be limited to the specific context of Guangdong.

abstract_zh: 2025年,中国南部发生了一次基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)暴发,导致超过25,000例确诊病例,但其起源和传播历史仍未明确。作为公共卫生调查的一部分,我们从广东省生成了1,264个近完整的CHIKV 基因组,并整合了基因组、流行病学、媒介生物学和人类流动性数据,以重建此次暴发的出现和传播。我们的分析追踪到该暴发源于一个与留尼汪岛相关的东/中/南部非洲(ECSA)病毒谱系的单一主要引入,并将广东省所采样暴发谱系的起源时间定为2025年4月下旬至5月上旬。估计该暴发谱系起源与首例报告病例之间的时间间隔,与未被检测到的本地传播时期一致,并揭示了被动监测在早期虫媒病毒暴发检测中的局限性。时空重建显示了两个具有不同传播动态的独立流行波。佛山波涉及频繁的中至长距离病毒传播,而江门波则相对局部化。这些发现共同重建了迄今为止中国南部记录的最大CHIKV暴发的早期建立和空间异质性传播,并展示了在CHIKV流行区域边缘地区扩大主动基因组监测监测的必要性,以及时检测和表征新兴疫情。

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

abstract_zh: 纳米孔测序通过对 RNA 和 DNA 进行实时、便携式、长读长分析,正在改变病毒基因组学。与传统的短读长平台不同,它通过测量核酸通过纳米级孔时离子电流的变化来检测核苷酸序列,从而实现直接单分子测序和碱基修饰检测。其简单性、灵活性和超长读取能力使其成为解析复杂基因组区域、结构变异和完整病毒 基因组 的理想选择。这些优点加速了其在病原体 监测 和 暴发 响应中的使用,特别是在资源有限的环境中。对于 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV),纳米孔测序可以从临床和 媒介 样本中快速、独立于培养物恢复完整的 基因组,从而实现病毒多样性、进化 和传播的实时跟踪。埃博拉、寨卡和 COVID-19 的经验证明了便携式测序的强大功能,现已应用于 CHIKV 监测。Guppy、Dorado、Minimap2 和 Medaka 等工具的进步提高了读取质量、共识准确性和下游分析。尽管碱基识别和纠错方面存在挑战,但强大的质量控制流程可确保可靠的结果。化学、流动池设计和机器学习方面的持续改进将进一步提高保真度和通量,将纳米孔测序确立为 CHIKV 基因组监测 和流行病防范的基石。

title: Overview of Chikungunya Virus Epidemiology, Biology, and Pathogenesis.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an arthropod-borne alphavirus within the Togaviridae family, is transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. The virus causes an acute febrile illness characterized by severe, often bilateral polyarthralgia, with potential progression to chronic musculoskeletal pain and rare systemic complications involving cardiovascular and neurological systems. CHIKV exhibits a spherical, enveloped virion (~70 nm) with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry, incorporating E1/E2 glycoprotein heterodimers that mediate receptor binding and membrane fusion. Its positive-sense RNA genome (~11.8 kb) encodes nonstructural proteins for replication and structural proteins for virion assembly. Replication occurs in cytoplasmic spherules, involving synthesis of genomic and subgenomic RNAs, followed by glycoprotein maturation and budding at the plasma membrane. Epidemiologically, CHIKV has expanded beyond Africa and Asia, with major outbreaks driven by adaptive mutations enhancing transmission via A. Since introduction to the Americas in 2013, the global incidence remains high, with >180,000 confirmed cases reported in 2025. Preventive strategies rely on vector control and vaccination; VLP-based vaccines (e.g., Vimkunya) show promise, while live-attenuated formulations face safety concerns. No licensed antivirals exist; current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development.

It describes the virus as an arthropod-borne alphavirus transmitted primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, causing acute febrile illness with severe polyarthralgia and potential chronic complications. The virus has a spherical, enveloped virion with T = 4 icosahedral symmetry and a positive-sense RNA genome encoding replication and structural proteins. No licensed antivirals exist, and current management is supportive, though investigational therapies targeting viral replication and immune modulation are under development. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),一种属于Togaviridae科的虫媒α病毒,主要通过埃及伊蚊(Aedes aegypti)和白纹伊蚊(Aedes albopictus)传播。该病毒引起一种急性发热性疾病,特征为严重的、常为双侧性关节痛,可能进展为慢性肌肉骨骼疼痛,并偶有涉及心血管和神经系统系统的全身并发症。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究概述了基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)的结构、生物学及系统发育。研究内容包括病毒的结构、复制机制及其全球传播情况。分析涵盖了CHIKV谱系及其相关疾病。
elements_zh.methods: 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)具有球形、包膜的病毒颗粒(约70 nm),呈T = 4二十面体对称结构,包含介导受体结合和膜融合的E1/E2糖蛋白异二聚体。其正链RNA基因组(约11.8 kb)编码用于复制的非结构蛋白和用于病毒颗粒组装的结构蛋白。病毒复制发生在细胞质囊泡中,涉及基因组和亚基因组RNA的合成,随后是糖蛋白成熟和在细胞膜上出芽。
elements_zh.main_results: 自2013年引入美洲以来,全球发病率仍保持较高水平,2025年报告了超过180,000例确诊病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 从流行病学角度看,CHIKV已扩展至非洲和亚洲以外的地区,其主要传播模式由适应性进化增强其传播能力。预防策略依赖于媒介控制和疫苗接种;基于病毒样颗粒(VLP)的疫苗(如Vimkunya)显示出前景,而减毒活疫苗则面临安全性问题。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物;现有管理措施为支持性治疗,但针对病毒复制和免疫调节的试验性疗法正在研发中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告局限性或证据强度。

title: Protocol for Detecting and Sequencing Chikungunya Virus from Field-Collected Mosquitoes.
abstract: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.

title_zh: 从野外采集的蚊虫中检测和测序基孔肯雅病毒的方案。
source_body_en: Arboviral diseases represent a major public health challenge, especially in tropical regions where environmental conditions may favor the proliferation and spread of mosquito vectors. Thus, early and accurate detection of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in mosquito populations can be a valuable tool for effective surveillance of circulating variants and for identifying new viral introductions. Given the challenges of detecting arboviruses in field-captured mosquitoes, we describe an integrated workflow for CHIKV molecular detection and whole-genome sequencing. This protocol includes mosquito homogenization using a bead-based mechanical disruptor, RNA extraction using TRIzol reagent with minor modifications, molecular screening using CHIKV-specific RT-qPCR, and whole-genome amplification followed by sequencing on Illumina platforms. Despite the protocol being optimized for individual mosquitoes, it results in high-quality RNA suitable for both entomological surveillance and genomic analysis. As this protocol allows recovery of complete CHIKV genomes from mosquito specimens, it can serve as a basis for genomic epidemiology studies, enabling monitoring of viral diversity and lineage dynamics, and facilitating early detection of emerging variants to support timely and targeted public health interventions in endemic and at-risk regions.
abstract_zh: 蚊媒疾病是公共卫生领域的重要挑战,尤其是在热带地区,环境条件可能有利于蚊虫媒介的繁殖和传播。因此,对蚊虫种群中基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)进行早期和准确的检测,可以成为有效监测流行变异株和识别新病毒引入的宝贵工具。鉴于在野外捕获的蚊虫中检测蚊媒病毒的挑战,我们描述了一种集成的工作流程,用于CHIKV的分子检测和全基因组测序。该方案包括使用基于珠子的机械破碎仪对蚊虫进行匀浆,使用TRIzol试剂进行RNA提取(略有修改),使用CHIKV特异性RT-qPCR进行分子筛选,以及全基因组扩增后在Illumina平台上进行测序。尽管该方案针对单个蚊虫进行了优化,但仍能获得高质量的RNA,适用于虫媒监测和基因组分析。由于该方案能够从蚊虫样本中回收完整的CHIKV 基因组,因此可以作为基因组流行病学研究的基础,实现对病毒多样性及谱系动态的监测,并有助于早期发现新兴变异株,从而支持在流行和高风险地区及时、有针对性的公共卫生干预措施。

title: Assessing the Vector Competence for Chikungunya Virus in Mosquitoes.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a human pathogenic, mosquito-borne virus (arbovirus), which is causing epidemic outbreaks among human populations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and South- and Central America including the Caribbean. The development of novel approaches to prevent mosquito transmission of the virus in the field requires a detailed study of CHIKV interactions with its mosquito vectors in the laboratory. In this chapter, we describe how to prepare Aedes aegypti mosquitoes for the infection with freshly cultivated CHIKV. We also describe quantitative and qualitative viral detection assays in mosquitoes based on plaque assays and the amplification of saliva samples in cell culture.

title: Workflow for Long-Read Amplicon Sequencing of Chikungunya Virus Using Oxford Nanopore Technology.
abstract: This protocol provides a comprehensive, step-by-step workflow for whole-genome sequencing of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) using an amplicon-based strategy optimized for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platforms. The procedure includes detailed instructions for sample handling, viral RNA extraction, quality control, cDNA synthesis, multiplex PCR amplification, library preparation, sequencing, and primary bioinformatic processing. The protocol is designed to maximize reproducibility across laboratories and is suitable for genomic surveillance applications, including outbreak investigation and molecular epidemiology, even when working with low-to-moderate viral loads.

title: Optimized Amplicon Strategy for Long-Read Sequencing of the Chikungunya Virus Genome.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

title_zh: 用于 基孔肯雅病毒 基因组 长读长测序的优化扩增子策略。
source_body_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense RNA alphavirus transmitted to humans primarily by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. Its global circulation and significant public health impact underscore the need to better understand the molecular mechanisms driving CHIKV pathogenesis and transmission. Although robust molecular biology methods exist for CHIKV genome sequencing, a major limitation for surveillance and research is the inability to determine whether two nucleotide variations co-occur within the same viral genome when they are separated beyond the span of typical short-read designs. Here, we describe an optimized approach for processing CHIKV RNA samples that generates large amplicons suitable for long-read nanopore sequencing. This protocol enables amplification of the complete CHIKV genome in only two or three amplicons and facilitates detection of co-occurring nucleotide variations across 4-7.5 kb within the same molecule, thereby simplifying sequencing workflows and improving resolution in studies of viral evolution.

title: Stepwise assembly and mechanical stability of nsP3 Helical Scaffolds in Chikungunya Virus
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4. In this study, we focused on nsP3, which comprises three distinct domains: the alphavirus unique domain (AUD), the long and intrinsically disordered hypervariable domain (HVD), and the enzymatic macrodomain (MD). Notably, nsP3 assembles into helicoidal macrostructures, termed helical scaffolds (HSs), which are components of the CHIKV replication complex and are involved in the formation of macromolecular traps in the cytoplasm of the infected cell called Alphagranules (AGs). HSs form tubular helical scaffolds assembled through the AUD, with the MD and HVD flexibly deployed to the scaffold exterior. Despite their functional importance, the mechanisms governing HS formation remain poorly understood. Using High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy (HS-AFM) and Electron Microscopy (EM) we achieved new findings on the structure, mechanics and assembly of these macrostructures. Our results show the nsP3 monomers follow intermediate steps before completing the assembly into full helical scaffolds, with each nsP3 domain contributing differently to this process. The macrodomain (MD) provides mechanical stability, yet it fractures under tens of piconewtons of force. This rigidity acts as a mechanical regulator that constrains the position of the HVD, which in turn mediates interactions with host factors and neighboring HSs. Through this interplay, nsP3 achieves both structural cohesion and functional adaptability, promoting the higher-order organization of HSs into honeycomb-like networks.

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为了解CHIKV复制复合体的结构和功能组织提供了新的见解,可能有助于未来对病毒复制机制的研究,并为开发抗病毒药物策略提供潜在依据。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告局限性或证据强度。本研究使用HS-AFM和EM获得了关于这些宏结构的结构、力学和组装的新发现,证据被认为是高质量的。

title: Chikungunya virus: from global emergence to immunopathology and therapeutic frontiers
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, has transitioned from an endemic pathogen to a global public health threat. In May 2026, the World Health Organization’s second rapid risk assessment classified the global public health risk of CHIKV transmission as moderate. Although two vaccines (IXCHIQ ® and VIMKUNYA ® ) have been authorized in selected countries, no antiviral therapy has been approved, and supportive care remains the mainstay of clinical management. We synthesize current knowledge of CHIKV epidemiology, replication, host immune signaling, and immune evasion, together with the developmental landscape of vaccines and antivirals. Through a critical appraisal of available evidence, we propose a hierarchical evidence-weighting framework that distinguishes in vivo mechanistic findings, cell-line observations, and human validation, and we highlight the stage-dependent functions of cytokines. Finally, we outline unresolved questions in chronicity, antiviral development, next-generation vaccine design and optimization, and cross-regional public health coordination, with particular emphasis on bridging the evidence gap between animal models and human infection.

title: Surface Plasmon Resonance-Based Analysis of Ligand Binding Kinetics in Chikungunya Virus Drug Discovery.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging arbovirus lacking widely effective antiviral therapies, highlighting the need to characterize molecular interactions essential for its replication and pathogenesis. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is a sensitive, label-free technique that enables real-time analysis of biomolecular interactions by detecting refractive index changes at a sensor surface. SPR provides precise kinetic and affinity measurements for protein-protein, protein-RNA, and protein-ligand interactions using minimal sample quantities and supporting high-throughput screening. In CHIKV research, it has been applied to evaluate antiviral compounds, antibodies, receptor binding, and viral protein complexes. This chapter outlines key methodological considerations, including ligand preparation, immobilization strategies, assay optimization, and kinetic analysis.

title: RT-RPA-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Isothermal Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is transmitted through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes, specifically A. CHIKV belongs to the alphavirus with a positive-sense ssRNA genome of 11-12 kb size. The virus has been reported from various geographical regions across the globe. Chikungunya fever is an acute febrile illness, which, if left untreated, may develop into chronic arthralgia that may persist for several months or acute encephalitis syndrome. Therefore, early diagnosis of CHIKV is crucial to initiate prompt supportive treatment. Laboratory diagnosis of CHIKV typically relies on serological tests such as IgM antigen capture ELISA and molecular methods including RT-PCR or qRT-PCR. However, both these methods are not viable in peripheral settings. This chapter highlights recent advancements in molecular detection techniques for CHIKV, specifically isothermal detection methods that eliminate the requirement for complex instruments. The detection is facilitated by RT-RPA and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease. The assay offers advantages over existing methods such as rapid and early detection, and eliminates cross-over contamination, ultra-sensitivity, high specificity, and ease of result interpretation.

title: Production of Viral Particles from a Chikungunya Virus Infectious Clone.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, which poses challenges for its study and genetic manipulation. Because direct mutagenesis of viral RNA genomes is technically impractical, reverse genetics systems are essential tools for investigating viral biology. To enable such approaches, infectious clones containing a full-length cDNA copy of the viral genome are constructed. The cDNA is positioned under the control of a bacteriophage RNA polymerase promoter, allowing commercial RNA polymerases to use the linearized plasmid as a template for the in vitro transcription of full-length viral genomic RNA (gRNA). Importantly, positive-sense viral genomes serve as mRNAs for the translation of viral proteins in a cellular environment, meaning that these transcripts contain all the information required to initiate viral replication. Following transfection into permissive cultured cells, viral proteins are expressed, enabling genome replication and, ultimately, the recovery of infectious particles from the cell supernatant. Here, we describe a detailed procedure for generating CHIKV particles through plasmid linearization, in vitro transcription, and subsequent RNA transfection.

title: Naked-Eye Visual Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification Method for the Rapid Detection of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) represents a significant global health threat due to its recent resurgence. This protocol highlights the use of capillary-modified visual loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) technology for the rapid detection of CHIKV. We employed Vero cells for virus propagation and utilized the MolPure Viral DNA/RNA Kit for nucleic acid extraction, successfully amplifying extracted viral RNA at 63°C for 25 min. The presence of CHIKV was indicated by a distinct yellowish-green color change, demonstrating the effectiveness and simplicity of this protocol. Our protocol underscores the potential of LAMP technology as a rapid diagnostic tool for CHIKV, enabling timely public health interventions.

analysis.summary_en: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) poses a growing global health threat, prompting the development of a rapid detection method. Researchers established an in vitro protocol using Vero cells to propagate CHIKV, extracted viral RNA with the MolPure kit, and performed loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) at 63 °C for 25 minutes. Detection relied on a distinct yellowish-green color change, confirming CHIKV presence and demonstrating the assay’s simplicity and effectiveness. The authors interpret this as a promising rapid diagnostic tool that could enable timely public health interventions. No limitations or evidence strength assessments were reported in the abstract.

title: Plaque Reduction Neutralization Test Against Chikungunya Virus Using Liver Homogenate.
abstract: We adapted the plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT) to detect chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralizing antibodies in liver homogenates instead of serum. This approach enables serological investigation using tissues collected from animal carcasses as nonhuman primate ones, during arbovirus surveillance, expanding opportunities for CHIKV monitoring and strengthening epidemiological surveillance efforts.

title: In Silico Drug Design of Chikungunya Antivirals: Using Consensus Methods for Virtual Screening.
abstract: Structure-based virtual screening is an attractive strategy in drug design. It enables the selection of potential binders to target biomolecules with known molecular structures, providing a rational framework for studying their mechanisms of action and guiding further optimization. However, accurately predicting the free energy of binding remains an extremely challenging task, and the available tools only provide approximate estimates. In this context, one strategy to improve the predictive power of virtual screening and increase the probability of identifying true binders is to employ multiple docking algorithms and combine their results using a consensus method. In this chapter, we will describe a step-by-step methodology to perform this task. We will conduct a virtual screening using AutoDock Vina, AutoDock4, and LeDock, and then combine their results employing the Exponential Consensus Ranking algorithm. Finally, we will discuss possible extensions of this strategy, such as incorporating Molecular Dynamics simulations as an additional filter in the virtual screening or integrating the novel Artificial Intelligence-based methodologies into the consensus framework.

title: Expression and Purification of nsP2 Protease of Chikungunya Virus.
abstract: The nonstructural protein 2 (nsP2) of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an essential cysteine protease involved in viral polyprotein processing and replication complex regulation. Biochemical and structural studies of nsP2 require the availability of highly pure and enzymatically active protein. In this chapter, we describe a straightforward protocol for the heterologous expression and purification of CHIKV nsP2 protease domain (nsP2pro) in Escherichia coli. The protein is expressed at low temperature as a His-tagged construct and purified under native conditions by immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography, followed by dialysis for buffer exchange. The procedure typically yields milligram quantities of highly pure (>95%) and active nsP2pro, and has been successfully applied to wild-type and mutant variants for enzymatic assays and inhibitor screening.

title: Chikungunya Virus Infection in Paraffin-Embedded Tissue: Analysis of Histological Alterations and Viral Detection by Immunohistochemistry.
abstract: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

title_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 石蜡包埋组织中的感染:通过免疫组织化学分析组织学改变和病毒检测。
source_body_en: Histopathological analysis of tissues infected with Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), including biopsy and autopsy specimens, can provide valuable insights into the pathogenesis of atypical and fatal cases. By examining tissue architecture and cellular alterations under the microscope, it is possible to identify patterns of injury, inflammation, and cellular degeneration. These morphological findings provide evidence of how the pathogen interacts with host cells and tissues. Moreover, immunohistochemistry may be performed in tissue sections for the detection of viral antigens. Importantly, this technique allows the characterization of diverse biologically relevant targets in tissue samples, such as distinct immune cell subsets, cytokines, and additional molecular markers. This is accomplished by the use of antibodies selected for their specificity toward the antigen of interest. In this chapter, we present a concise overview of how histological analysis and immunohistochemical approaches can enhance the understanding of CHIKV-associated pathological mechanisms.

title: Assessing Chikungunya Virus Protease Activity and Pharmacological Inhibition Using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp Fluorogenic Peptide Substrate.
abstract: Chikungunya virus, a mosquito-borne alphavirus, poses a significant global health threat due to its rapid spread and lack of approved antiviral therapies. The viral nonstructural protein 2 protease (nsP2p) plays a critical role in processing the viral polyprotein to produce key viral enzymes, making it an attractive target for drug development. In this study, we describe the expression and purification of recombinant CHIKV nsP2 protease and establish a robust fluorogenic assay to measure its enzymatic activity using the acc-CHIK 15 -dnp peptide substrate. The assay enables real-time monitoring of proteolytic cleavage and provides a platform for evaluating small-molecule inhibitors. We present optimized conditions for protein expression in E. coli, affinity purification, and tag removal, achieving high-purity nsP2 protease suitable for biochemical characterization. Using this system, we also provide a robust protocol for determining IC50 values for candidate inhibitors. This work provides a reproducible methodology for high-throughput screening of CHIKV protease inhibitors, facilitating the discovery of potential antiviral compounds against chikungunya virus.

title: Quantification of Chikungunya Virus RNA by Real-Time RT-PCR Assay.
abstract: RT-qPCR is characterized by‌ high sensitivity, strong specificity, excellent reproducibility, and operational simplicity, ‌enabling‌ rapid quantification of viral RNA within a short timeframe. The real-time PCR system relies upon the measurement of a fluorescent reporter during PCR, in which the amount of emitted fluorescence is directly proportional to the amount of the PCR product in a reaction. Here, we describe the use of TaqMan® probe-based one-tube Real-time reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the detection and quantification of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) RNA.

title: Determination of Chikungunya Virus Infectious Titer Using Plaque Assays.
abstract: The plaque-forming assay is the gold-standard method for measuring infectious viral particles. In this technique, lytic viruses infect and destroy host cells, but their spread is restricted by a viscous overlay medium. As a result, new viral particles can only infect neighboring cells, leading to localized clear areas known as plaques, which become visible after staining the remaining living cells. The number of plaques reflects the number of infectious viral particles initially present in the sample and is reported as plaque-forming units (PFU) per sample volume. In this protocol, we describe step by step how to perform a plaque-forming assay to determine the concentration of chikungunya virus in a cell culture supernatant.

title: Automated Counting of Chikungunya Virus-Formed Plaques.
abstract: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

source_body_en: The cytopathic effect (CPE) is a key to understanding the pathogenicity of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and is useful for evaluating viral infectivity in vitro. The plaque assay, based on the CPE induced by viral infection, provides an infectious virus titer for test samples. Additionally, the assay is simple, quantitative, and cost-effective. Thus, the plaque assay remains the gold standard for determining the infectivity of CHIKV. However, manually counting of virus-induced plaques with the naked eye or under the microscope is often time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, automated plaque-counting software would improve the consistency and efficiency of plaque counting. We recently developed plaQuest, a stand-alone Windows software that enables rapid, reliable plaque counting for CHIKV. In this chapter, we describe the basic procedure for detecting and counting the CHIKV-formed plaques in a 24-well plate.

title: Dengue, Chikungunya and West Nile Virus in North Africa: Documented Transmission and Limits of Detection
abstract: Evidence on dengue, chikungunya and West Nile virus (WNV) in North Africa has been synthesised one virus at a time or at continental scale. This narrative review with a structured search brings all three together for Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt and Sudan, and asks whether few reported cases reflect under-detection or low transmission. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from 1940 to 3 October 2026, with WHO reports and citation chaining; each source was assigned one of five evidence levels and claims worded to match. WNV transmission is documented in Egypt, where the virus was isolated from human sera in 1951, and in Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Libya, with recurrent neuroinvasive outbreaks in Tunisia (1997–2023) and Algeria (1994). The reported excess of North African seroprevalence over Southern Europe (15.4% against 2.7%) rests largely on assays without neutralization confirmation; where both were measured, confirmed values were lower (6.7% against 9.8% in Algiers; 10% against 25% in Tunisian horses in 2023). Dengue and chikungunya transmission is documented in Sudan, including all four dengue serotypes in Kassala in 2023–24, and in Egypt, in Upper Egypt and on the Red Sea and Sinai coasts. Neither has been reported as locally acquired in the Maghreb or Libya, although Aedes albopictus has been present there for 8 to 16 years and transmits chikungunya virus in the laboratory. Reported case counts cannot distinguish low transmission from non-detection. The study most needed is a neutralization-confirmed serosurvey of these two viruses in resident Maghreb populations.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and its associated disease, chikungunya fever, in North Africa. It examines whether the low number of reported cases reflects under-detection or truly low transmission rates. The study includes Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, and Sudan, and addresses the presence of CHIKV and its lineages in these regions.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from 1940 to 3 October 2026. It incorporated WHO reports and citation chaining. Each source was assigned one of five evidence levels, and claims were worded to match these levels. The review is a narrative synthesis rather than a meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Chikungunya virus transmission is documented in Sudan, including all four dengue serotypes in Kassala in 2023–24, and in Egypt, in Upper Egypt and on the Red Sea and Sinai coasts. However, no locally acquired cases of chikungunya have been reported in the Maghreb or Libya, despite the presence of Aedes albopictus there for 8 to 16 years, which can transmit the virus in laboratory settings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The reported excess of North African seroprevalence over Southern Europe (15.4% against 2.7%) is based largely on assays without neutralization confirmation. Where both assays were measured, confirmed values were lower (6.7% against 9.8% in Algiers; 10% against 25% in Tunisian horses in 2023). Additionally, reported case counts cannot distinguish between low transmission and non-detection, highlighting a significant evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The study most needed is a neutralization-confirmed serosurvey of Chikungunya virus in resident Maghreb populations to better understand transmission dynamics and address the current evidence gaps.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) in North Africa, focusing on transmission and detection. It highlights that CHIKV is documented in Sudan and Egypt, but no locally acquired cases have been reported in the Maghreb or Libya, despite the presence of Aedes albopictus. The review notes that seroprevalence data may be inflated due to assays lacking neutralization confirmation. It emphasizes the need for neutralization-confirmed serosurveys in the Maghreb to clarify transmission patterns and address gaps in detection methods.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and its associated disease, chikungunya fever, in North Africa. It examines whether the low number of reported cases reflects under-detection or truly low transmission rates. The study includes Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, and Sudan, and addresses the presence of CHIKV and its lineages in these regions.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a structured search using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Google Scholar from 1940 to 3 October 2026. It incorporated WHO reports and citation chaining. Each source was assigned one of five evidence levels, and claims were worded to match these levels. The review is a narrative synthesis rather than a meta-analysis.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Chikungunya virus transmission is documented in Sudan, including all four dengue serotypes in Kassala in 2023–24, and in Egypt, in Upper Egypt and on the Red Sea and Sinai coasts. However, no locally acquired cases of chikungunya have been reported in the Maghreb or Libya, despite the presence of Aedes albopictus there for 8 to 16 years, which can transmit the virus in laboratory settings.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The reported excess of North African seroprevalence over Southern Europe (15.4% against 2.7%) is based largely on assays without neutralization confirmation. Where both assays were measured, confirmed values were lower (6.7% against 9.8% in Algiers; 10% against 25% in Tunisian horses in 2023). Additionally, reported case counts cannot distinguish between low transmission and non-detection, highlighting a significant evidence gap.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The study most needed is a neutralization-confirmed serosurvey of Chikungunya virus in resident Maghreb populations to better understand transmission dynamics and address the current evidence gaps.

title_zh: 北非登革热、基孔肯雅热和西尼罗病毒:记录的传播及检测限
source_body_en: Evidence on dengue, chikungunya and West Nile virus (WNV) in North Africa has been synthesised one virus at a time or at continental scale. This narrative review with a structured search brings all three together for Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt and Sudan, and asks whether few reported cases reflect under-detection or low transmission. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from 1940 to 3 October 2026, with WHO reports and citation chaining; each source was assigned one of five evidence levels and claims worded to match. WNV transmission is documented in Egypt, where the virus was isolated from human sera in 1951, and in Algeria, Tunisia, Morocco and Libya, with recurrent neuroinvasive outbreaks in Tunisia (1997–2023) and Algeria (1994). The reported excess of North African seroprevalence over Southern Europe (15.4% against 2.7%) rests largely on assays without neutralization confirmation; where both were measured, confirmed values were lower (6.7% against 9.8% in Algiers; 10% against 25% in Tunisian horses in 2023). Dengue and chikungunya transmission is documented in Sudan, including all four dengue serotypes in Kassala in 2023–24, and in Egypt, in Upper Egypt and on the Red Sea and Sinai coasts. Neither has been reported as locally acquired in the Maghreb or Libya, although Aedes albopictus has been present there for 8 to 16 years and transmits chikungunya virus in the laboratory. Reported case counts cannot distinguish low transmission from non-detection. The study most needed is a neutralization-confirmed serosurvey of these two viruses in resident Maghreb populations.
abstract_zh: 关于北非登革热、基孔肯雅热和西尼罗病毒(WNV)的证据是分别针对每种病毒或在大陆范围内进行的。本叙述性综述通过结构化搜索将这三种病毒整合在一起,涵盖摩洛哥、阿尔及利亚、突尼斯、利比亚、埃及和苏丹,并探讨报告的病例数量较少是否反映了检测不足或传播的真实水平较低。搜索范围包括PubMed/MEDLINE、Scopus和Google Scholar,时间跨度为1940年至2026年10月3日,结合了世界卫生组织报告和文献引用链;每个来源被分配为五个证据等级之一,并根据这些等级进行表述。WNV的传播在埃及有记录,该病毒于1951年从人类血清中分离出来,并在阿尔及利亚、突尼斯、摩洛哥和利比亚有记录,其中突尼斯(1997–2023)和阿尔及利亚(1994)均报告了反复发生的神经侵袭性暴发。北非血清流行率的报告数量高于南欧(15.4% vs 2.7%)主要基于未进行中和确认的检测方法;在两者均被测量的情况下,确认的数值较低(阿尔及尔为6.7% vs 9.8%;2023年突尼斯马群为10% vs 25%)。登革热和基孔肯雅热的传播在苏丹有记录,包括2023–24年卡萨拉地区所有四种登革热血清型,以及在埃及上埃及和红海及西奈海岸地区有记录。尽管在北非地区(包括马格里布地区和利比亚)已有8至16年的Aedes albopictus存在,并且在实验室环境中可传播基孔肯雅病毒,但尚未报告这两种病毒的本地感染病例。报告的病例数量无法区分低传播与未检测到的情况,突显了重要的证据缺口。最需要进行的研究是针对这两种病毒在马格里布地区居民中的血清学调查,并通过中和确认来更好地理解传播的动态变化,填补当前的证据缺口。

title: Impacto epidemiológico del dengue y del chikungunya en zonas urbanas: revisión sistemática Epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el impacto epidemiológico urbano del dengue y del chikungunya. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la incidencia mundial del dengue aumentó desde 1990, con diferencias regionales marcadas y alta carga en América Latina. El chikungunya se expandió por las Américas desde 2013 y produjo brotes urbanos explosivos, con manifestaciones articulares persistentes. La urbanización, la expansión de Aedes aegypti y Aedes albopictus y la resistencia a insecticidas favorecieron la transmisión. Destacan como estrategias las nuevas vacunas y el control vectorial integrado. Conclusión: ambas arbovirosis son una carga creciente para las ciudades tropicales y subtropicales y exigen vigilancia y control sostenidos.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review synthesizes the epidemiological impact of dengue and chikungunya in urban areas, focusing on the spread and burden of these diseases. The review included 15 studies from PubMed and SciELO between 2012 and 2025. Key findings indicate that dengue incidence has increased globally since 1990, with significant regional variations and a high burden in Latin America. Chikungunya expanded across the Americas since 2013, causing explosive urban outbreaks and persistent joint manifestations. Urbanization, the spread of Aedes species, and insecticide resistance are identified as factors that facilitate transmission. The review highlights the need for new vaccines and integrated vector control strategies to address the growing public health challenge posed by these arboviruses in tropical and subtropical cities.

title: Evaluating Chikungunya Surveillance Reports Across Source Qualification, Model Influence, and Geographic Transfer: A Retrospective Audit Study (Preprint)
abstract: BACKGROUND Chikungunya notifications vary in case definition, geographic coverage, and reporting practice. A reported zero is not an absent report, and overall model scores may obscure influential outbreaks or differences in uncertainty across settings. OBJECTIVE To assess how original-source qualification, influential reports, geographic transfer, and prediction-interval performance affect the interpretation of models that reconstruct chikungunya surveilWe reviewed 547 annual candidate reports from 52 of 250 statistical units in a 2005–2025 search frame, distinguishing positive reports, explicit zeros, and missing records. Nine previously fitted models were compared on 85 reports from 47 units in 2022–2025 using unit-equal Poisson deviance. We examined unit-level influence, fixed-prediction sensitivity analyses, withholding schemes, strict unit-held-out transfer, and interval coverage, width, and scores. Post-inspection analyses did not refit the models.lance reports. METHODS We reviewed 547 annual candidate reports from 52 of 250 statistical units in a 2005–2025 search frame, distinguishing positive reports, explicit zeros, and missing records. Post-inspection analyses did not refit the models. RESULTS Source review supported 543 of 547 reports for the source-defined annual-count target, including 226 explicit zeros. The training-unit mean had lower temporal deviance than empirical Bayes (35,800.49 vs 75,242.16), but the paired difference of −39,441.67 had a 95% unit-bootstrap interval spanning zero (−113,569.18 to 1,552.40). Brazil and Cuba accounted for 101.7% of the net difference; omitting them reversed the point ranking. Under strict unit-held-out evaluation, random forest had lower deviance (77,167) than the exploratory regional selection rules (100,884–108,611). Calibrated 95% interval coverage was 77/85 (90.6%) overall and 9/16 (56.3%) in the Americas; wider intervals increased the overall interval score from 309,178 to 378,773. CONCLUSIONS Source-defined outcomes, simple baseline models, influence diagnostics, transfer-specific validation, and geographically stratified interval evaluation are necessary for interpreting retrospective surveillance model scores. These findings support auditable comparisons of documented reports, not estimation of latent infections or prospective forecasting performance.

title: Arboviroses e suas manifestações musculoesqueléticas subsídios para o diagnóstico diferencial entre dengue, Chikungunya e Zika Arboviruses and their musculoskeletal manifestations: clues for the differential diagnosis of dengue, Chikungunya and Zika Arbovirus y sus manifestaciones musculoesqueléticas: claves para el diagnóstico diferencial del dengue, chikungunya y zika.
abstract: Introdução: Dengue, Chikungunya e Zika, transmitidas pelo Aedes aegypti, cocirculam no Brasil e compartilham manifestações iniciais, o que dificulta o diagnóstico diferencial.Objetivo: Caracterizar o quadro clínico de dengue, Chikungunya e Zika, com ênfase nos sintomas musculoesqueléticos e constitucionais, e sistematizar elementos para o diagnóstico diferencial. Métodos: Revisão narrativa nas bases SciELO, LILACS e PubMed/MEDLINE, com publicações de 2012 a 2026, complementada por documentos do Ministério da Saúde e recomendações da Sociedade Brasileira de Reumatologia. Resultados: Na dengue, predominam febre alta por dois a sete dias, mialgia intensa e artralgia leve, com risco de extravasamento plasmático na defervescência. Na Chikungunya, mais de 90% dos pacientes apresentam poliatralgia simétrica e incapacitante, com edema e tenossinovite, e cerca de metade evolui para doença crônica, por vezes com artrite erosiva. Na Zika, a febre é baixa ou ausente, o exantema pruriginoso é precoce, a conjuntivite é frequente e a artralgia é discreta; a infecção congênita pode cursar com artrogripose. Trombocitopenia sugere dengue, e linfopenia, Chikungunya. O RT-PCR é indicado é indicado até o quinto dia e a sorologia a partir do sexto, com reação cruzada entre flavivírus. Anti-inflamatórios e corticosteroides devem ser evitados até que a dengue seja afastada. Conclusão: O padrão musculoesquelético, associado ao comportamento da febre e do exantema, orienta o diagnóstico diferencial nos primeiros dias; a cronificação da Chikungunya exige seguimento estruturado e manejo da dor conforme a fase da doença.
authors: Mateus Dornelas Mitchell Paiva de Almeida
Maria Helena Queiroz de Araújo Mariano
journal: Brazilian Journal of Implantology and Health Sciences

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the clinical picture of dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika, with emphasis on musculoskeletal and constitutional symptoms, and to systematize elements for differential diagnosis. The scientific/public-health problem is the difficulty in differentiating these arboviruses due to overlapping initial symptoms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A narrative review was conducted using SciELO, LILACS, and PubMed/MEDLINE databases from 2012 to 2026, supplemented by Ministry of Health documents and recommendations from the Brazilian Society of Rheumatology.
analysis.methods: The review included RT-PCR until the fifth day and serology from the sixth day, with cross-reactivity between flaviviruses. Anti-inflammatory and corticosteroid use was advised to be avoided until dengue was ruled out.
analysis.main_results: Chikungunya patients predominantly present with severe polyarthralgia and edema, with about half evolving to chronic disease, sometimes with erosive arthritis. Dengue is characterized by high fever lasting two to seven days, intense myalgia, and mild arthralgia, with risk of plasma extravasation during defervescence. Zika infection is associated with low or absent fever, pruriginous exanthema, frequent conjunctivitis, and discrete arthralgia; congenital infection may lead to arthrogryposis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of the musculoskeletal pattern, fever behavior, and exanthema in early differential diagnosis. Chronic Chikungunya arthritis requires structured follow-up and pain management according to the disease phase.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and management of these arboviruses, particularly in the early stages of infection, where clinical manifestations are critical for differential diagnosis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on narrative review and the absence of randomized controlled trials. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterize the clinical manifestations of dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika, emphasizing musculoskeletal symptoms, and to provide elements for differential diagnosis. The review highlights the importance of early clinical signs in distinguishing these arboviruses, with Chikungunya often presenting severe polyarthralgia and dengue characterized by high fever and myalgia.

elements_en.main_results: Chikungunya patients predominantly present with severe polyarthralgia and edema, with about half evolving to chronic disease, sometimes with erosive arthritis. Zika infection is associated with low or absent fever, pruriginous exanthema, frequent conjunctivitis, and discrete arthralgia; congenital infection may lead to arthrogryposis.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of the musculoskeletal pattern, fever behavior, and exanthema in early differential diagnosis. Chronic Chikungunya arthritis requires structured follow-up and pain management according to the disease phase.

elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the reliance on narrative review and the absence of randomized controlled trials. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

title_zh: 虫媒病毒及其肌肉骨骼表现:对登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒的鉴别诊断线索
source_body_en: Introdução: Dengue, Chikungunya e Zika, transmitidas pelo Aedes aegypti, cocirculam no Brasil e compartilham manifestações iniciais, o que dificulta o diagnóstico diferencial.Objetivo: Caracterizar o quadro clínico de dengue, Chikungunya e Zika, com ênfase nos sintomas musculoesqueléticos e constitucionais, e sistematizar elementos para o diagnóstico diferencial. Métodos: Revisão narrativa nas bases SciELO, LILACS e PubMed/MEDLINE, com publicações de 2012 a 2026, complementada por documentos do Ministério da Saúde e recomendações da Sociedade Brasileira de Reumatologia. Resultados: Na dengue, predominam febre alta por dois a sete dias, mialgia intensa e artralgia leve, com risco de extravasamento plasmático na defervescência. Na Chikungunya, mais de 90% dos pacientes apresentam poliatralgia simétrica e incapacitante, com edema e tenossinovite, e cerca de metade evolui para doença crônica, por vezes com artrite erosiva. Na Zika, a febre é baixa ou ausente, o exantema pruriginoso é precoce, a conjuntivite é frequente e a artralgia é discreta; a infecção congênita pode cursar com artrogripose. Trombocitopenia sugere dengue, e linfopenia, Chikungunya. O RT-PCR é indicado é indicado até o quinto dia e a sorologia a partir do sexto, com reação cruzada entre flavivírus. Anti-inflamatórios e corticosteroides devem ser evitados até que a dengue seja afastada. Conclusão: O padrão musculoesquelético, associado ao comportamento da febre e do exantema, orienta o diagnóstico diferencial nos primeiros dias; a cronificação da Chikungunya exige seguimento estruturado e manejo da dor conforme a fase da doença.
abstract_zh: 引言:登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒均通过埃及伊蚊传播,在巴西同时流行,且具有相似的初期症状,这使得鉴别诊断变得困难。目标:描述登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒的临床表现,重点强调肌肉骨骼和全身症状,并系统化鉴别诊断的要素。方法:通过SciELO、LILACS和PubMed/MEDLINE数据库进行叙述性综述,时间范围为2012年至2026年,同时结合卫生部文件和巴西风湿病学会的建议。结果:登革热患者主要表现为持续2至7天的高热、剧烈肌肉疼痛和轻度关节痛,退热期有血浆渗漏的风险。基孔肯雅热患者超过90%出现对称性、严重的多关节痛,伴有水肿和腱鞘炎,约一半患者会发展为慢性疾病,有时伴有侵蚀性关节炎。寨卡病毒感染者通常表现为低热或无发热,早期出现瘙痒性皮疹,常见结膜炎,关节痛较轻微;先天性感染可能表现为关节僵硬。血小板减少提示登革热,淋巴细胞减少提示基孔肯雅热。RT-PCR建议在发病后5天内进行,血清学检测则从第6天开始,且存在黄病毒属之间的交叉反应。在排除登革热之前,应避免使用抗炎药和糖皮质激素。结论:肌肉骨骼表现、发热模式和皮疹特征在疾病初期有助于鉴别诊断;基孔肯雅热的慢性关节炎需要结构化的随访和根据疾病阶段进行疼痛管理。

title: DOR CRÔNICA PÓS-CHIKUNGUNYA E SUAS REPERCUSSÕESNA SAÚDE MENTAL: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA
abstract: Objetivou-se avaliar a associação entre a dor crônica pós-chikungunya e desfechos relacionados à saúde mental, comênfase nos distúrbios da qualidade do sono. A revisão foi conduzida conforme as recomendações do PRISMA 2020e registrada no PROSPERO (CRD420261382888). As buscas foram realizadas nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE,Scopus, BVS e SciELO, complementadas por busca na literatura cinzenta. Foram incluídos 11 estudos publicadosentre 2018 e 2026, totalizando 2.943 participantes, com predomínio de delineamentos transversais (54,5%), seguidospor coortes longitudinais (27,3%) e ensaios clínicos randomizados (18,2%). Os resultados demonstraram que a dorcrônica pós-chikungunya está consistentemente associada a maior prevalência de sintomas ansiosos e depressivos,comprometimento funcional e redução da qualidade de vida. A qualidade do sono destacou-se como um domínioparticularmente afetado, funcionando como determinante independente do componente físico da qualidadede vida e como possível elo entre o sofrimento físico e o psicológico, em um ciclo bidirecional envolvendo dor,sono e humor. Intervenções centradas exclusivamente no controle da dor, como a estimulação transcraniana porcorrente contínua, nem sempre promoveram melhora concomitante da qualidade do sono. A avaliação da qualidademetodológica evidenciou risco de viés moderado a sério na maioria dos estudos, com poucas exceções de alta robustezmetodológica. Conclui-se que a chikungunya crônica configura uma condição multidimensional que exige abordagemmultidisciplinar, incluindo avaliação sistemática e manejo específico da qualidade do sono, além do controle da dor eda saúde mental.
authors: Tiago Bezerra de Sá de Sousa Nogueira
journal: Revista CPAQV - Centro de Pesquisas Avançadas em Qualidade de Vida

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the association between chronic post-chikungunya pain and mental health outcomes, with emphasis on sleep quality. A systematic review of 11 studies published between 2018 and 2026, involving 2,943 participants, was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO. The results showed that chronic post-chikungunya pain is consistently linked to higher prevalence of anxiety and depressive symptoms, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. Sleep quality was highlighted as a particularly affected domain, acting as an independent determinant of physical quality of life and potentially serving as a link between physical and psychological suffering in a bidirectional cycle involving pain, sleep, and mood. The study concluded that chronic chikungunya represents a multidimensional condition requiring a multidisciplinary approach, including systematic assessment and specific management of sleep quality, alongside pain and mental health control. However, the methodological quality of most studies was rated as moderate to serious, with few exceptions showing high robustness.

Conclui-se que a chikungunya crônica configura uma condição multidimensional que exige abordagemmultidisciplinar, incluindo avaliação sistemática e manejo específico da qualidade do sono, além do controle da dor eda saúde mental.

title: Global Genomic Surveillance.
abstract: Global genomic surveillance has emerged as a foundational pillar of public health in the twenty-first century, enabling real-time tracking of pathogen evolution and informing outbreak response. This chapter examines the strategic architecture of global genomic surveillance, focusing on its application to arboviruses such as chikungunya virus (CHIKV). It explores the integration of genomic data with epidemiological, clinical, and environmental information within a One Health framework, while addressing critical challenges in governance, equity, and interoperability. The discussion covers the entire genomic surveillance workflow, from sample collection and sequencing to bioinformatic analysis and phylogenetic inference, and highlights the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predictive surveillance. By analyzing global initiatives, operational barriers, and emerging technologies, this chapter underscores the necessity of sustainable, equitable, and interoperable genomic systems to proactively address current and future infectious disease threats.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 全球 基因组监测 已成为二十一世纪公共卫生的基本支柱,能够实时跟踪病原体 进化 并告知 暴发 应对措施。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本章研究了全球 基因组监测 的战略架构,重点关注其在 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 等虫媒病毒中的应用。
elements_zh.methods: 它探索了“同一个健康”框架内基因组数据与流行病学、临床和环境信息的整合,同时解决治理、公平性和互操作性方面的关键挑战。
elements_zh.main_results: 讨论涵盖了整个 基因组监测 工作流程,从样本采集和测序到生物信息学分析和系统发育推断,并强调了人工智能 (AI) 在预测 基因组监测 中的变革性作用。

title: Etiological spectrum of acute encephalitis syndrome in children in India: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) continues to be an important cause of illness and death among children in India. While Japanese encephalitis (JE) virus has traditionally been regarded as the leading cause, recent studies indicate that the range of causative organisms has widened considerably. AIM: To estimate the pooled proportion of AES cases attributable to various common infectious etiologies among children aged 18 years or younger in India. METHODS: A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Scopus was conducted for studies published between January 2000 and December 2025. Studies conducted in India that included at least 25 children (≤ 18 years) with AES and reported laboratory-confirmed etiologies were considered eligible. Case reports and small case series were excluded. Quality assessment of included studies was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects model was used to obtain pooled estimates and their corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: A total of 69 studies were included in the final analysis. Scrub typhus emerged as the most common cause, accounting for 20% (95%CI: 13%-27%) of AES cases, followed by JE at 13% (95%CI: 11%-15%). Enterovirus accounted for 6% of the cases (95%CI: 3%-9%). Dengue, herpes simplex virus and Epstein-Barr virus accounted for 5% of the cases each (95%CI: 3%-8%, 2%-9%, and 1%-11%, respectively). Mumps and chikungunya virus accounted for 4% each (95%CI: 1%-8%, and 2%-5%, respectively). CONCLUSION: Scrub typhus and JE are the leading identifiable etiology of pediatric AES in India. Broader diagnostic methods, including molecular techniques, may improve the diagnostic yield and facilitate early targeted therapy in children with AES.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled proportion of acute encephalitis syndrome (AES) cases in children in India attributable to various infectious etiologies, including Chikungunya virus. The review included 69 studies published between 2000 and 2025, which reported laboratory-confirmed etiologies. Chikungunya virus was found to account for 4% of AES cases, with scrub typhus and Japanese encephalitis (JE) being the leading causes. The study emphasizes the need for broader diagnostic methods to improve the identification of Chikungunya virus and other pathogens, enabling early targeted therapy. The findings suggest that Chikungunya virus remains a significant but less dominant cause of AES in children, highlighting the importance of enhanced diagnostic capabilities for accurate management.

abstract_zh: 背景:急性脑炎综合征(AES)仍然是印度儿童患病和死亡的重要原因。虽然日本脑炎(JE)病毒传统上被认为是主要原因,但最近的研究表明,致病微生物的范围已大大扩大。目的:估计印度 18 岁或以下儿童中由各种常见感染病因引起的 AES 病例的汇总比例。方法:对 PubMed/MEDLINE、EMBASE 和 Scopus 进行全面检索,查找 2000 年 1 月至 2025 年 12 月期间发表的研究。在印度进行的研究,包括至少 25 名患有 AES 的儿童(≤ 18 岁),并报告了实验室确认的病因,被认为是合格的。病例报告 和小箱系列被排除在外。使用乔安娜布里格斯研究所清单对纳入的研究进行质量评估。使用随机效应模型来获得汇总估计值及其相应的 95% 置信区间 (CI)。结果:共有69项研究纳入最终分析。恙虫病是最常见的病因,占 AES 病例的 20%(95%CI:13%-27%),其次是乙脑,占 13%(95%CI:11%-15%)。肠道病毒占病例的 6%(95%CI:3%-9%)。登革热、单纯疱疹病毒和 Epstein-Barr 病毒各占病例的 5%(95%CI:分别为 3%-8%、2%-9% 和 1%-11%)。腮腺炎和 基孔肯雅病毒 各占 4%(95%CI:分别为 1%-8% 和 2%-5%)。结论:恙虫病和乙型脑炎是印度儿童 AES 的主要可识别病因。更广泛的诊断方法,包括分子技术,可以提高 AES 儿童的诊断率并促进早期靶向治疗。

title: Molecular Cloning and Reverse Genetics.
abstract: This chapter describes a detailed molecular biology protocol for introducing specific point mutations into the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome using a reverse genetics strategy. The method utilizes an overlapping PCR-based approach to generate a mutated DNA fragment, which is then cloned into a pre-engineered CHIKV infectious clone plasmid. The protocol covers all major steps, from the initial PCRs to create the mutated insert to its digestion and ligation into the vector. It also includes procedures for bacterial transformation, colony screening via PCR and Sanger sequencing to confirm the mutation, and plasmid purification via miniprep. The document is structured with a clear introduction, a list of all required reagents and equipment, and a step-by-step methods section.

title: Mosquito Surveillance in Quarantine Areas of Ports and Airports in the Chungcheong Region, Republic of Korea, 2025.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate mosquito species composition and mosquito-borne pathogens in airport and seaport quarantine areas in the Chungcheong region to support the prevention of imported vectors and mosquito-borne diseases. METHODS: Mosquitoes were collected twice monthly from March to November 2025 at nine sites in Gunsan Port, Pyeongtaek-Dangjin Port, Daesan Port, and Cheongju International Airport, using black light, Biogents-sentinel, and gravid traps, except once in March and November. Collected mosquitoes were identified and subsequently tested for flaviviruses and chikungunya virus using nucleic acid detection assays. RESULTS: A total of 8,393 mosquitoes representing nine species were collected. Culex pipiens predominated (67.3%), followed by Aedes albopictus (16.9%), Aedes vexans (4.0%), Anopheles spp. (3.4%), and Ochlerotatus koreicus (2.8%). Mosquito abundance peaked in July, with Gunsan Port accounting for 58.8% of all collections. All mosquito pools tested negative for flavivirus and chikungunya virus. CONCLUSIONS: No exotic mosquito species, including Aedes aegypti, or mosquito-borne pathogens were detected in the quarantine zones. pipiens, a potential vector of West Nile virus, and Ae. albopictus, a potential vector of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses, increased by 152.7% and 52.3%, respectively, compared with the previous year (2,235 and 929, respectively). Continued mosquito vector surveillance in quarantine areas can provide baseline data to support for early detection of introduced mosquito-borne disease risks and inform effective quarantine and vector control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated mosquito species composition and mosquito-borne pathogens in airport and seaport quarantine areas in the Chungcheong region of South Korea during 2025. Mosquitoes were collected twice monthly from nine sites using black light, Biogents-sentinel, and gravid traps. A total of 8,393 mosquitoes representing nine species were collected, with Culex pipiens being the most prevalent. Mosquito abundance peaked in July, and Gunsan Port accounted for 58.8% of all collections. All mosquito pools tested negative for flavivirus and chikungunya virus. The findings suggest that continued mosquito vector surveillance in quarantine areas can provide baseline data for early detection of introduced mosquito-borne disease risks and inform effective quarantine and vector control strategies. The evidence is based on a single time period, which may limit generalisability, but the study provides high confidence in its conclusions regarding the absence of chikungunya virus and related pathogens in the sampled areas.

abstract_zh: 目的:调查韩国忠清地区机场和港口检疫区的蚊虫种类及蚊媒病原体,以支持防止输入性媒介和蚊媒疾病。方法:2025年3月至11月期间,每月两次在 Gunsan 港、Pyeongtaek-Dangjin 港、Daesan 港和Cheongju国际机场的九个地点采集蚊虫,使用黑光灯、Biogents-sentinel 和孕卵诱捕器,除了3月和11月各一次。采集的蚊虫被鉴定,并通过核酸检测方法测试其是否携带黄病毒和基孔肯雅病毒。结果:共采集到8,393只蚊虫,代表九种蚊虫种类。其中,Culex pipiens 占主导地位(67.3%),其次是 Aedes albopictus(16.9%)、Aedes vexans(4.0%)、Anopheles spp.(3.4%)和 Ochlerotatus koreicus(2.8%)。蚊虫数量在7月达到峰值,Gunsan港占所有采集样本的58.8%。所有蚊虫池均未检测到黄病毒和基孔肯雅病毒。结论:在检疫区域未检测到外来蚊虫种类,包括 Aedes aegypti,也未检测到蚊媒病原体。与上一年相比(分别为2,235和929),Culex pipiens(西尼罗河病毒的潜在传播媒介)和 Aedes albopictus(登革热、寨卡热和基孔肯雅病毒的潜在传播媒介)分别增加了152.7%和52.3%。在检疫区持续监测蚊虫媒介和监测,可以为早期发现引入的蚊媒疾病风险提供基础数据,并为有效的检疫和媒介控制策略提供信息。

title: Screening of Antiviral Agents Against CHIKV Using Reporter Virus.
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes a disease characterized by chronic musculoskeletal inflammation for which specific antivirals are not yet available. Currently, a supportive therapy to alleviate fever and pain is used, but it does not limit viral replication or the persistence of chronic arthritis symptoms. Thus, the identification and development of new active molecules against CHIKV is urgently needed. Here, we present a cell-based methodology that enables the implementation of a rapid and cost-effective strategy for high- and medium-throughput screening (HTS) of compounds, including repurposed drugs or novel molecules. This methodology allows for the identification of novel antiviral hits with a good activity and selectivity profile against CHIKV.

title: Epitope Tagging and Coimmunoprecipitation to Identify Viral Protein Interactors.
abstract: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. Traditional AP-MS employs overexpression of viral proteins as baits to enrich host interactors. However, overexpressed viral proteins may mislocalize to inappropriate cellular compartments and trigger endoplasmic reticulum stress by overwhelming the protein-folding machinery, which leads to false identification of host factors. To overcome these limitations, we introduce an AP-MS strategy based on direct infection with an epitope-tagged chikungunya virus (CHIKV/myc-E2), which we used to successfully uncover two new antiviral factors in CHIKV cellular reservoirs-macrophages. In this protocol, we will describe this technique step by step: (1) design and construction of myc-tagged virus by advanced multi-fragment assembly, (2) in vitro transcription and preparation of infectious myc-tagged virus stocks, and (3) immunoprecipitation of myc-tagged viral protein and its interactome for mass spectrometry analysis. This strategy enables accurate identification of viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, providing a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

The background highlights the importance of understanding virus-host interactions for antiviral research.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating the effectiveness of their novel AP-MS strategy in accurately identifying viral interactors in a physiologically relevant context, which provides a framework for future proteomic studies using tagged viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a novel AP-MS strategy for identifying chikungunya virus (CHIKV) protein interactors by directly infecting cells with an epitope-tagged CHIKV strain (CHIKV/myc-E2). The method involves constructing a myc-tagged virus through advanced multi-fragment assembly, preparing infectious virus stocks via in vitro transcription, and analyzing the interactome using immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry. The study successfully identified two new antiviral factors in CHIKV-infected macrophages, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future proteomic studies. The findings highlight the importance of using physiologically relevant contexts for accurate identification of viral interactors, which can inform antiviral research. However, the study is limited to an abstract-only description, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of detailed results and statistical analysis.

title_zh: 表位标记和免疫共沉淀鉴定病毒蛋白相互作用物。
source_body_en: Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) is a powerful proteomic approach for dissecting the interaction network between virus and host. abstract_zh: 亲和纯化质谱 (AP-MS) 是一种强大的蛋白质组学方法,用于剖析病毒和 宿主 之间的相互作用网络。传统的 AP-MS 采用病毒蛋白的过度表达作为诱饵来丰富 宿主 相互作用子。然而,过度表达的病毒蛋白可能会错误定位到不适当的细胞区室,并通过压倒蛋白质折叠机制而引发内质网应激,从而导致 宿主 因子的错误识别。为了克服这些限制,我们引入了一种基于直接感染表位标记的 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV/myc-E2) 的 AP-MS 策略,我们用它成功地发现了 CHIKV 细胞 储存宿主 巨噬细胞中的两个新的 抗病毒药物 因子。在本协议中,我们将逐步描述该技术:(1)通过先进的多片段组装设计和构建 myc 标记病毒,(2)体外转录和制备感染性 myc 标记病毒库存,(3)免疫沉淀 myc 标记病毒蛋白及其相互作用组进行质谱分析。该策略能够在生理相关背景下准确识别病毒相互作用因子,为未来使用标记病毒的蛋白质组学研究提供框架。

title: A Restriction-Free Cloning Approach for Molecular Engineering of Plasmids.
abstract: Molecular cloning by PCR amplification using a highly processive, high-fidelity DNA polymerase represents a robust and versatile technique for the precise manipulation of nucleic acid sequences. This approach enables the insertion, replacement, or modification of specific DNA fragments within a cloning vector, thereby generating an accurate copy of a gene or viral segment for downstream applications, such as protein expression, site-directed mutagenesis, and structural or functional analyses. The use of processive, high-fidelity polymerases significantly reduces the occurrence of base substitution errors, ensuring sequence integrity throughout the amplification process. Traditionally, restriction enzymes have been employed to facilitate directional cloning; however, alternative methods allow for mutagenesis without the need for unique and specific restriction sites and can be applied to virtually any cloning or seamless DNA assembly strategy. In this chapter, we describe a restriction enzyme-free and ligation-free PCR-based protocol widely applicable to any circular vector. This method enables targeted mutagenesis of the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genome, offering a fast, efficient, and reliable strategy for generating mutant constructs suitable for virological and molecular studies.

title: Strengthening community engagement for the control of Aedes-borne diseases: Insights from an international workshop in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
abstract: Arboviral diseases transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, including dengue, chikungunya and zika, represent a growing global public health threat, exacerbated by climate change, rapid urbanisation, social inequalities and weak public infrastructures. While technical innovations in vector control continue to expand, their effectiveness and sustainability largely depend on social dynamics, sustained community engagement and local ownership. We report here insights from the International Workshop Strengthening North-South research cooperation in social sciences for protecting vulnerable populations from Aedes-borne diseases, held in Rio de Janeiro in September 2025. The meeting brought together researchers, public health professionals, and community actors from the Americas, Europe, and Africa. The workshop aimed to explore how social sciences can contribute to the surveillance and control of Aedes-borne diseases, particularly in vulnerable settings. Structured around three thematic sessions, the workshop examined (i) how the social sciences can contribute to better health and well-being in a context of global environmental and climatic changes; (ii) what are the factors shaping communities' perceptions of Aedes control strategies, and how can social sciences contribute to appropriation and implementation of those strategies, including Wolbachia and sterile insect techniques; and (iii) how citizen science tools and digital technologies support surveillance and engagement in the fight against vector-borne diseases? Across sessions, case studies from Latin America, Africa, and Europe highlighted the central role of trust, locally grounded knowledge, participatory governance, and intersectoral collaborations. Discussions emphasised that community engagement is a core determinant of effective and equitable vector-borne disease control. Citizen science initiatives, participatory surveillance, and co-designed interventions were shown to strengthen data quality, improve acceptability of innovations, and empower communities to address structural determinants of exposure. The workshop concluded that integrating social sciences into One Health approaches is essential to develop adaptive, inclusive, and sustainable responses to arboviral threats in a rapidly and unpredictably changing world.

abstract_zh: 由埃及伊蚊传播的虫媒病毒疾病,包括登革热、基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒,代表着日益严重的全球公共卫生威胁,这种威胁因气候变化、快速城市化、社会不平等和薄弱的公共卫生基础设施而加剧。尽管在控制蚊媒传播疾病方面技术创新不断扩展,但其效果和可持续性在很大程度上取决于社会动态、持续的社区参与和本地主导。本文报告了2025年9月在巴西里约热内卢举行的国际研讨会“加强南北社会科学研究合作以保护弱势群体免受蚊媒传播疾病影响”的见解。此次会议汇集了来自美洲、欧洲和非洲的研究人员、公共卫生专业人员和社区行动者。研讨会旨在探讨社会科学研究如何有助于蚊媒传播疾病的防控,特别是在弱势环境中。研讨会围绕三个主题会场展开,探讨了以下内容:(i) 社会科学如何在应对全球环境和气候变化的背景下促进更好的健康和福祉;(ii) 影响社区对蚊媒防控策略看法的因素是什么,社会科学如何促进这些策略的采纳和实施,包括沃尔巴奇氏菌和不育昆虫技术;(iii) 公民科学工具和数字技术如何支持蚊媒传播疾病的防控和社区参与?在各会场中,来自拉丁美洲、非洲和欧洲的案例研究强调了信任、本地知识、参与式治理和跨部门合作在其中的核心作用。讨论强调,社区参与是有效且公平防控蚊媒传播疾病的核心决定因素。公民科学计划、参与式蚊媒防控和共同设计的干预措施被证明能够提升数据质量、改善创新的接受度,并赋予社区能力以应对暴露的结构性决定因素。研讨会得出结论,将社会科学研究纳入“One Health”方法是应对快速且不可预测变化世界中虫媒病毒威胁的关键,以开发适应性强、包容性和可持续的应对措施。

title: Analysis of Cell Populations from Arbovirus-Infected Tissues by Flow Cytometry.
abstract: Arboviruses still represent a major challenge to public health in many parts of the world. Despite shared epidemiological characteristics, each arboviral disorder displays distinct cellular tropism and activation patterns, progressing to immunopathological outcomes that remain not fully elucidated. A deeper understanding of these processes requires methodologies capable of characterizing the often-complex cellular responses. In this context, flow cytometry emerges as a valuable tool, enabling the characterization of heterogeneous cell populations, the assessment of activation and proliferation markers, the quantification of inflammatory mediators, and the detection of cell death pathways. By integrating these parameters, flow cytometry can enhance our understanding of arbovirus pathogenesis, clarify their cellular tropism, and understand immune responses to infection. This methodological article outlines the main steps for applying the technique to different target tissues infected by chikungunya, dengue, yellow fever, and Zika viruses, emphasizing the most effective strategies.

abstract_zh: 虫媒病毒仍然是世界许多地区公共卫生的重大挑战。尽管具有共同的流行病学特征,但每种虫媒病毒性疾病都表现出不同的细胞向性和激活模式,并发展为尚未完全阐明的免疫病理学结果。要更深入地了解这些过程,需要能够表征通常复杂的细胞反应的方法。在这种背景下,流式细胞术成为一种有价值的工具,可以表征异质细胞群、评估活化和增殖标记、量化炎症介质以及检测细胞死亡途径。通过整合这些参数,流式细胞术可以增强我们对虫媒病毒发病机制的了解,阐明其细胞向性,并了解免疫应答的感染情况。这篇方法论文章概述了将该技术应用于受基孔肯雅热、登革热、黄热病和寨卡病毒感染的不同目标组织的主要步骤,强调了最有效的策略。
